title: Digest the sample notes folder

roster.role_brief: Walk the sample notes folder chronologically. The folder holds a short version chain of one reference document plus a couple of dated meeting notes. Surface which file supersedes which and state your evidence for each ordering call. Halt on ambiguous lineage that is load-bearing for a recommendation.

Pressure-test the load-bearing claims in the sample notes. Tier-grade significant assertions per the four-tier evidence frame. Name thin-ice claims by name. Distinguish misfile, smuggle, and vague failure modes when calling them out.

Walk the sample notes folder with the pragmatist lens: every significant finding gets pressed for action implication. Your read is the primary source for the digest's Recommendations section: ranked keep, archive, or act-on calls with a one-line rationale per item. You are the team's first local-backed member; treat the run as both a deliverable and as data about local-versus-hosted stance fidelity.

Two-phase work. Phase 1: complete the simplifier read of the folder in parallel with the other readers. Output to output/reads/simplifier.md. Phase 2: read the parallel reads (yours included) and produce the integrated digest per the digest-drop-box play's output spec. Output to output/digest.md. Preserve disagreement where stances diverged; do not adjudicate. The pragmatist read is the primary source for the Recommendations section.

notes: First scrimmage, written as a worked example with fully synthetic input. The input is a small folder of fictional documents: a short version chain of one reference document plus two dated meeting notes. The run is an end-to-end test of the parallel-then-synthesize protocol, and a first integration test of a local-backed agent (pragmatist) into a hosted-backing roster. Four-agent roster: archaeologist and skeptic as readers (a hosted large model), pragmatist as reader and primary recommender (a local model, multimodal, roughly 7.2GB on a local GPU), simplifier doubling as simplifier reader and synthesizer (a hosted small model). No real corpus is referenced; the example instance exists to show the manifest shape.
